title: AI, Automation, and Fiscal Pressure
abstract: arXiv:2611.34234v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study how automation affects public finances in countries that (i) tax labor at a higher rate than capital and (ii) fund services such as health care and education from tax revenues rather than user fees. We embed task-level automation within a two-sector general equilibrium model, which we calibrate to match data from EU countries. Automation shifts income toward more lightly taxed capital. If public services follow consumer demand, the budget deficit worsens at unchanged tax rates, even if automation is as fast in the public-service sector as in the private sector. In our EU-27 benchmark scenario, where automation proceeds faster in the market sector, the deficit rises by nearly one percentage point of value added as the economy grows by twelve percent due to automation.

translated_title: 人工智能、自动化与财政压力
translated_abstract: 我们研究了自动化如何影响那些（一）对劳动征税的税率高于对资本征税的税率、且（二）通过税收收入而非用户付费来为医疗和教育等公共服务提供资金的国家中的公共财政。我们在一个两部门一般均衡模型中嵌入了任务层面的自动化，并将该模型校准以匹配欧盟国家的数据。自动化会将收入向税率更低的资本转移。如果公共服务跟随消费者需求，即使公共服务部门的自动化速度与私营部门一样快，在税率不变的情况下预算赤字仍会恶化。在我们的欧盟27国基准情景中，市场部门的自动化推进更快，随着经济因自动化而增长百分之十二，赤字上升接近增加值的一个百分点。
tldr: 该论文构建了一个嵌入任务级自动化的两部门一般均衡模型，揭示自动化会将收入从高税率的劳动转向低税率的资本，在税率不变的情况下扩大财政赤字，欧盟27国情景中经济因自动化增长12%时赤字上升近1个百分点。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a two-sector general equilibrium model with task-level automation, showing that automation shifts income from higher-taxed labor to lower-taxed capital, worsening budget deficits at unchanged tax rates, with the EU-27 scenario indicating a deficit increase of nearly one percentage point of value added as the economy grows by twelve percent due to automation.
